comment: Worst stack frame per source file, for every file clippy measures above
threshold_bytes. Keyed by file because a large_stack_frames primary span is
not always a function signature, so a function name is not a stable key, and
because the worst frame in a file bounds every other frame in it: a lesser
frame that grew past this number would become the new worst and be caught.
Growth past a file's number by more than its tolerance band is refused.
Shrinkage passes and is reported; so does movement inside the band. Banking
a new baseline happens on main in the stack-frame banking job, never on a
pull request, so no branch rewrites the measurement it is judged by.
The band is max(tolerance_bytes, number * tolerance_fraction). It is margin,
not measured noise: the same tree was measured four times, once on a build
host and three times by this gate's own CI job, and all 112 files agreed to
the byte. Observed run-to-run variance was zero. The band is held against a
future toolchain that is less reproducible than this one, and the byte floor
exists so a frame just over threshold_bytes still gets a usable band.
A budgeted file with no diagnostic passes only when this run's compiler
artifact depfiles prove its source was compiled. Then its worst frame is
below the measurement floor. Without that proof, absence is refused:
a skipped crate must never read as a successful shrink.
Separately, any frame within near_ceiling_fraction of ceiling_bytes is
refused outright regardless of its budget, because that is the band where a
nested descent overflows a worker stack. Frames already inside that band
when the gate landed are listed as exceptions with an expiry and an owner.
